newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAA starts SAfrica-Sweden service with full load.
newsitem.headline: SAA starts SAfrica-Sweden service with full load.

text.p: South African Airways (SAA) ushered in its Stockholm-Johannesburg freight service with a full cargo load, and its Nordic sales agent said it expected to fill the carrier again this week.
SAA on October 13 began operating an Airbus 300 between Sweden and South Africa, scheduled to leave Stockholm's Arlanda international airport on Sunday afternoons.

Kim Schultz, vice president of the carrier's cargo sales agent Maersk Air, said the airplane flew as scheduled, carrying 33 tonnes of cargo which included agricultural machinery, electronic goods and spare car parts.
"Bookings normally arrive late Thursday or early Friday. Indications we have at the moment show it looks good."
Schultz said full capacity of the flight was 33 to 34 tonnes because of the flight's distance and weather conditions.
Christer Holst, Arlanda's cargo development manager, said the airport was talking to other carriers about adding more direct cargo flights.
"Image-wise it means a lot to get a direct connection to another continent," Holst told Reuters.
"We are working to get a direct connection to the United States."
